question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away this Kaula teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents vast wealth
The comparison sets up a valuation of the teaching
inference: Even one who could amass an ocean full of jewels should not trade this teaching for it.
uncertainties: The form akretuṃ is irregular and likely corrupt for a form of krī/kartuṃ
plain_english: Even if one had the means to make an ocean filled with jewels.
